title: Smooth stack morphisms are preserved by composition and base change
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\mathcal Z$ be algebraic stacks over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. A morphism of these stacks is smooth if it is smooth on smooth scheme charts, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. If $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $g:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ are smooth, then $g\circ f$ is smooth. If $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is smooth and $h:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$ is any morphism, then the projection $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth. These assertions include scheme and algebraic-space sources and targets, with representable smooth morphisms interpreted on scheme base changes [def-trf-algebraic-space]. No quasi-compactness, separation, finite-type or flatness condition is imposed on $h$.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $W\to\mathcal Z$, then scheme atlases $V\to\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal Z}W$ and $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. These fibre products are algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], so the atlases exist by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. The representable calculus [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus] shows that $V\to\mathcal Y$ and $U\to\mathcal X$ are smooth and surjective: each is an atlas followed by a base change of the preceding atlas. Condition (A) of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion], applied first to $g$ and then to $f$, gives smooth scheme maps $V\to W$ and $U\to V$; the induced relative chart maps are exactly the atlases chosen above. These maps of schemes are smooth in the algebraic-space sense of the criterion; by [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], applied with the property smooth, which is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], they are smooth as scheme morphisms. Their composite $U\to W$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition], hence smooth in the criterion's sense by the same comparison. The diagram $U\to W$ over $g\circ f$ has smooth vertical maps and surjective source map. Condition (B) of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion] therefore proves the composition assertion.

proof.text: For arbitrary $h:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$, choose atlases $V\to\mathcal Y$, $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, and $V'\to\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. Existence uses [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products, def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. The presentation criterion [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion](A) makes $U\to V$ a smooth scheme map. Put $E=U\times_VV'$, a scheme by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $U\to\mathcal X$ is smooth surjective as in step 1. Since $U\to V$ is a map of algebraic spaces, it is representable and the representable comparison of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion] makes it a smooth representable map; its projection $E\to V'$ is therefore smooth by the arbitrary representable base-change clause of [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Set $P=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$. Associating the tuples and their specified isomorphisms in the $2$-fibre products [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] identifies $E$ with $(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V')\times_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V}U$. Thus $E\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$ is a base change of the chosen atlas $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. Also $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V'\simeq P\times_{\mathcal Z}V'$. The map $V'\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth surjective as the atlas followed by the base change of $V\to\mathcal Y$; hence so is $E\to P$ by the same representable calculus. The diagram $E\to V'$ over $P\to\mathcal Z$ has smooth vertical maps and a surjective source map. Criterion (B) proves smoothness of $P\to\mathcal Z$. Only atlas maps were assumed smooth; no property of $h$ was used.

proof.text: The algebraic-space comparison in [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion] identifies the smooth chart condition with ordinary smoothness when source and target are spaces; its representable comparison identifies it with the scheme base-change test. Scheme smoothness agrees with this chart condition by [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] applied to the smooth case of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Therefore the preceding arguments also give exactly the scheme, algebraic-space and representable interpretations in the statement.
